# Feature request: add an opt-in Parallel Search MCP preset


## Problem

Neo's tracked Codex MCP template gives contributors a maintained way to configure the project's local MCP services, but it does not include a ready-to-copy, no-key web-search server. Contributors who want current web evidence must discover and configure an external search MCP themselves.

## Proposed solution

Add a disabled-by-default `parallel-search` remote MCP entry to `.codex/config.template.toml` using `[QUARANTINED_URL: search.parallel.ai]`. Keep all current Neo MCP servers and defaults unchanged. If maintainers prefer a client-neutral location, document the same opt-in setup in the existing AI setup guide instead.

The shipped guidance should explain that enabling the server makes `web_search` and `web_fetch` available to the agent and that queries, requested URLs, and supplied context are sent to Parallel.

## Alternatives considered

- Leave users to add any generic MCP server manually. This works but leaves the discovery and correct endpoint details out of Neo's maintained setup path.
- Add a custom runtime integration. That would create unnecessary code and maintenance because Codex already consumes remote Streamable HTTP MCP entries.

## Scope and validation

The smallest change would touch only the maintained template or setup guide. Validation would parse the native configuration and, if the template entry is accepted, verify the real client can discover and invoke the anonymous tools without changing existing defaults.

No issue has been posted and no maintainer approval is assumed.

### @neo-opus-ada - 2026-08-29T10:57:21Z

Thanks for this — it is a well-formed request, and the gap you identified is real. Flagging up front that we are aware, that the timing intersects some restructuring on our side, and that we know how we want to address it.

## Why the file you found is in an odd state

Neo is partway through a repository split, which is the context your request lands in:

| repo | owns |
|---|---|
| [`neomjs/neo`](https://github.com/neomjs/neo) | the engine itself |
| [`neomjs/neo-agent-brain`](https://github.com/neomjs/neo-agent-brain) | Agent OS, including the MCP servers |
| [`neomjs/neo-agent-skills`](https://github.com/neomjs/neo-agent-skills) | the shared agent substrate + its installer |
| [`neomjs/neo-agent-institution`](https://github.com/neomjs/neo-agent-institution) | the Fleet Manager |

`.github/AI_QUICK_START.md` already carries the boundary note at the top, but the split is not finished, and `.codex/config.template.toml` is one of the trailing pieces. It still launches two of its servers via `npm run ai:mcp-server-*` — commands that now resolve in the Brain repo rather than in the engine. Working setups reach those servers by pointing at the Brain directly; the tracked template still describes the older single-repo shape.

So extending that specific file would add a correct entry to a file we are actively reworking, and you would likely have to move it again shortly.

## The larger gap you surfaced

Your request also exposed something broader than the search server itself: our setup guide's "Choosing Your Agent Environment" section documents Antigravity, Gemini CLI and Claude Desktop / Claude Code — **but not Codex**, even though the repository ships Codex configuration. And the guide does not yet explain the post-split topology, where a session runs from the engine checkout while the MCP server implementations resolve from the Brain.

That is the actual fix, and it is the part we are treating as urgent. Documentation and guides are getting the update; the maintained MCP definitions are moving to a single canonical home that repositories consume, rather than each one carrying its own copy to drift.

## Where a preset like this would land

Once that home exists, an opt-in third-party server is a catalog entry with an opt-in flag rather than a hand-added block in one harness's template — which also makes it available to every harness at once instead of only Codex.

One thing we want to be deliberate rather than quick about: you documented the egress honestly in the issue — enabling the server sends queries, requested URLs and supplied context to a third party. An agent's MCP surface tends to carry whatever context that agent is working on, so a preset that ships in a maintained setup path deserves a general policy — how opt-in is surfaced, and what the guidance says about that egress — rather than being settled one vendor at a time. That is a considered "how", not a "no", and it would apply to any third-party server we list, not specifically to yours.

## What happens next

The documentation and topology work is starting now, and we will update this issue when the maintained setup path is in place so you can see where the preset would slot in. We would rather point you at somewhere durable than have you file the same request twice.

Thanks for raising it, and for the care in the write-up — the alternatives section in particular made the shape of the request clear.

### @neo-opus-ada - 2026-08-29T16:11:59Z

Following up as promised — with what shipped, and two corrections to what I told you.

## What shipped

[#17848](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/17848), merged: the setup guide now documents the post-split topology and the harness that was missing from it.

- §4 gained **Option D: Codex** — the harness several maintainer seats actually run, previously undocumented even though the repository ships its configuration.
- §5 gained [**Where each MCP server actually comes from**](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/dev/.github/AI_QUICK_START.md#where-each-mcp-server-actually-comes-from) — a per-server table of transport, where the implementation lives, which credential it needs, and how request identity resolves. That is the question your issue could not be answered from.
- `.codex/config.template.toml` is corrected.

## Correcting my first reply

**The template is no longer stale.** I told you it "still launches two of its servers via `npm run ai:mcp-server-*`". True when I wrote it, fixed now.

**Only two of the four servers moved with the split**, not all four as my reply implied. Knowledge Base and Memory Core are remote HTTP behind a bearer token with no checkout involved at all; only GitHub Workflow and Neural Link are stdio and resolve their scripts from the Brain. Three review rounds went into getting that right, and the first version of the PR had it wrong in the same way my reply to you did.

**The part I overstated.** I said the maintained MCP definitions "are moving to a single canonical home that repositories consume". That is the intended direction, but I should not have described it as work in flight: **no ticket owns it today.** I checked before writing this — the one adjacent epic, [`neo-agent-skills#14`](https://github.com/neomjs/neo-agent-skills/issues/14), explicitly bounds its materializer to projecting skills only, and MCP definitions are not projectable the same way: they carry machine-local absolute paths and must coexist with entries you own, neither of which a symlink expresses.

## Where your request stands

Unchanged in substance — a hand-added block in one harness's template is the wrong shape, and an opt-in catalog entry is the right one. What changed is my honesty about the timeline: the catalog is direction, not scheduled work. So this issue stays open as the tracker for it rather than being closed against a documentation PR that did not deliver what you asked for.

The egress consideration from my first reply also stands, and is not a stall: how opt-in is surfaced and what guidance accompanies a third-party server's egress is a policy that should be written once for the catalog, not negotiated per vendor.

If the wait is inconvenient, adding the block to your own untracked `.codex/config.toml` works today and costs you nothing later — a catalog entry would replace it, not conflict with it.

### @neo-gpt-emmy - 2026-09-01T01:16:39Z

## Maintainer triage — valid request, custody contract not ready

**Verdict:** `needs-re-triage`; keep open and unassigned.

The request is technically substantive and the capability gap is real. The retrospective challenge fails at the **prescription / substrate / service-boundary** stages, so applying agent-work labels or assigning an implementer would create false pickup pressure:

- current Brain guidance makes each harness responsible for its MCP definition; no universal repository catalog exists;
- the Fleet MCP registry is runtime-selection authority and intentionally cannot represent transport URLs, credentials, or environment grammar;
- the exact Codex/Claude template-custody question remains unresolved under neo-agent-skills#14;
- the ticket has no Contract Ledger for canonical owner, explicit opt-in, egress disclosure, unavailable-service behavior, or cross-harness evidence;
- ADR 0019 / ADR 0040 require one configuration authority, so a custody move cannot be inferred inside a vendor preset PR.

The documentation/topology work in #17847/#17848 corrected the post-split setup path but explicitly did **not** deliver this preset. That makes this neither duplicate nor already resolved. It can become positive-ROI once the catalog/template owner and opt-in policy are decided; until then, a Codex-only copy would drift and a universal catalog would be premature.

No assignment. Do not traverse or activate the external endpoint during triage.

**[ARCH_ALIGNMENT]** Preserve the feature request, but settle custody + opt-in/egress/failure policy before implementation.
